questions.question: If a grammar has NO shift-reduce conflict under Canonical LR(1), can LALR(1) (built by merging states) introduce one?
questions.solutionApproach: No — merging states with the same LR(0) core never introduces a NEW shift-reduce conflict. It can only potentially introduce a new reduce-reduce conflict (since merged lookaheads can create ambiguity between which reduce to apply).
questions.answer: No — LALR merging never creates new shift-reduce conflicts, only possibly new reduce-reduce conflicts.

questions.question: Which is generally true: SLR(1) parser has MORE states than LALR(1), or the SAME number?
questions.solutionApproach: SAME number — both SLR(1) and LALR(1) are built on the underlying LR(0) automaton's state structure; they differ only in HOW lookaheads are computed/assigned for reduce decisions, not in the number of states.
questions.answer: Same number of states (both based on the LR(0) automaton).

questions.question: An LR parser is parsing input. Is it constructing a leftmost or rightmost derivation, and in what direction (forward or reverse)?
questions.solutionApproach: LR parsers construct the RIGHTMOST derivation, but trace it in REVERSE (starting from the input string and working back toward the start symbol via reductions).
